title: Casper and the Wolf
premise: Oscar Eriksen, a woman passing as a man to hide her gift of mapping living realms, keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things until a royal edict forces every gifted soul into the open or the grave. Her only allies are Casper, a wolf-shaped spirit bound to her by an old debt, and the guild's ragged found family of smugglers, forgers, and exiles. To save them all she must descend into the court beneath the mountain and steal back her own sold soul before the usurper's armies reach the free cities. She succeeds only by revealing her true name and nature—trading invisibility for loyalty—and returns not as a hidden cartographer but as the mapmaker who redraws the realm's borders herself.
about_author: Coral Crane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that no longer exist. She writes fantasy about people who survive by being mislabeled.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In the free city of Vellmark, Oscar balances the guild's ledgers, hiding her gift behind clerical drudgery while Casper, her wolf-spirit companion, haunts the warehouse rafters. A routine entry—a compass that points at regret—goes missing. The beat is quiet unease: the first sign that someone is reading her records too closely.

chapters.title: Edict of Ash
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Royal criers proclaim the Gifted Hunt: anyone with the sight must register or burn. The guild debates fleeing; Oscar argues they can forge their way through, concealing how much the edict terrifies her personally. Casper senses her fear and refuses to leave her side. Emotional beat: the fragile safety of her double life cracking open.

chapters.title: What the Wolf Remembers
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, rendered in strange, sensory prose. We learn Casper was once human, his soul sold to the court beneath the mountain long ago, and that he recognized Oscar's scent because her soul carries the same ledger-mark as his own contract. He has stayed with her out of debt and something warmer. Beat: devotion revealed, stakes deepened.

chapters.title: The Forger's Daughter
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Guild forger Sable Ives offers Oscar forged papers—but demands the truth in exchange, forcing Oscar to admit she's a woman with the gift, not the clerk 'Oskar.' Sable keeps the secret, binding them as co-conspirators. A hunt patrol nearly catches them; Casper draws it off. Beat: chosen family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: Borders That Breathe
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Using her gift in secret, Oscar maps the shifting passes toward the mountain, discovering the usurper's armies are being guided by another gifted traitor whose maps outpace hers. Jealousy and dread entwine: someone is selling the guild's routes. Beat: rising tension; her talent becomes both weapon and liability.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable uncovers proof that guildmaster Corvin has been trading maps to the crown in exchange for immunity—and that Oscar's name heads the list of souls promised to the mountain court. Torn between loyalty to Corvin, who raised him, and truth, Sable chooses truth. Beat: loyalty vs. theme crystallized in a secondary heart.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Salt Gate
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Confronted, Corvin admits he sold Oscar's soul years ago to buy the guild time, believing the court would never collect. Betrayed, Oscar flees with Casper and Sable as the army breaches Vellmark's salt gates. Beat: lowest point—the family fractured, home burning, identity stripped bare.

chapters.title: Down Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The three descend through a realm only Oscar can map, a labyrinth that reshapes itself around regret. They bargain with the court's pale steward: one soul may be reclaimed if another is left in its place. Casper quietly prepares to take it. Beat: love sharpened into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Dual POV climax. At the soul-vault, Oscar refuses Casper's sacrifice and instead offers the one thing worth more: her true name and her gift, freely given, redrawing the court's own boundaries so its power collapses inward. Casper's humanity flickers back; the usurper's armies lose their guiding maps mid-march. Beat: truth chosen over safety, at last.

chapters.title: Casper and the Wolf
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, closing where his began. Half-restored, neither wholly man nor wolf, he walks beside Oscar as she charts new borders for the free cities—not hidden now, but named. The guild rebuilds with Sable at its head. Final beat: found family reassembled, identity embraced, and a last line noting that some maps are promises, not records.
